title: Is there an accelerating nonspreading wave packet in the Schrödinger equation with higher even-order dispersions?
abstract: Probably not. For Airy-type initial data, although nearly all lobes accelerate, the principal lobe remains essentially stationary. Moreover, the overall wave packet gradually disperses.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the existence of self-accelerating, nonspreading wave packets in the Schrödinger equation modified by higher even-order dispersion terms. The authors prove that the characteristic self-acceleration observed in the standard quadratic case (Airy wave packet) does not generalize to the pure quartic case. Instead, the wave packet forms an accelerating caustic but always disperses over time.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether an accelerating, nonspreading wave packet solution exists for the Schrödinger equation when higher even-order dispersion (like quartic dispersion) is present, contrasting this with the known quadratic case.
main_result: The self-accelerating Airy phenomenon is specific to quadratic dispersion; for pure quartic or higher even-order dispersion, the wave packet exhibits an accelerating caustic but always disperses, contradicting the 'nonspreading' requirement.
method: The analysis uses ansatz solutions, Fourier transforms, and the method of numerical steepest descent to analyze the asymptotic behavior of the wave packet.
model_or_system: The model is the time-dependent Schrödinger equation with higher even-order dispersion, specifically $i\partial_t u = (\partial_x^{2n} + V(x, t))u$, analyzed for the free case ($V=0$).
key_observables: Caustic formation location ($x \sim t^{2n}$), wave packet amplitude decay rate ($\sim t^{-1/2n}$ for the principal lobe), and the existence of a nonspreading profile.
important_parameters: The order of the dispersion operator ($2n$), the initial data (e.g., $	ext{Ai}_{2n}(x)$), and the time $t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a general shape-preserving ansatz and relies on asymptotic expansions near caustics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the propagation of the wave packet for quartic and sixth-order dispersion, showing the accelerating caustic structure alongside the predicted dispersive decay of the amplitude.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the known quadratic case, then analyzes the general ansatz for higher even-order dispersion, deriving conditions that rule out rigidly accelerating solutions, and finally confirms dispersive decay rates for the free quartic case.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical constraints on the types of localized, non-dispersing wave dynamics possible in systems with higher-order dispersion, which is crucial for understanding wave propagation in nonlinear optics or quantum field theory models.
